title: A/P Detail: Date and Due Date sort oldest first, then newest first
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: One aging bucket on A/P Detail holds three bills with different dates and due dates.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • In the "1-30 days past due" bucket there are three open bills, {Document-A}, {Document-B} and {Document-C} for {Vendor-C}, {Vendor-A} and {Vendor-B} in that order (in name order these vendors read A, B, C): {Document-A} is dated 40 days ago, due 10 days ago, amount $300.00, open $50.00; {Document-B} is dated 20 days ago, due 20 days ago, amount $100.00, open $100.00; {Document-C} is dated 35 days ago, due 5 days ago, amount $200.00, open $150.00.
    For example: {Vendor-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-16 Alder, {Vendor-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-16 Birch, {Vendor-C} is ZZAUTOTEST S2-16 Cedar; {Document-A} is S1-101, {Document-B} is S1-99 and {Document-C} is S1-100 (the app assigns the real numbers; the dates and amounts are the ones that matter).
  • Starting screen: A/P Detail (Reports, then "A/P Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS PAYABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with the "1-30 days past due" bucket expanded.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "Date" header.
  2. Click the "Date" header again.
  3. Click the "Date" header a third time.
  4. Click the "Due Date" header.
  5. Click the "Due Date" header again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: rows inside each aging bucket sort by Date, oldest first: in the "1-30 days past due" bucket, {Document-A}, {Document-C}, {Document-B}.
  • Step 2: newest first: {Document-B}, {Document-C}, {Document-A}.
  • Step 3: oldest first again, as in step 1.
  • Step 4: rows inside each aging bucket sort by Due Date, oldest first: {Document-B}, {Document-A}, {Document-C}.
  • Step 5: newest first: {Document-C}, {Document-A}, {Document-B}.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S2-R1, A/P Detail and A/P Unpaid Invoices columns: “A/P Detail and A/P Unpaid Invoices: Date, Location (when shown), Transaction Type, No., Vendor Name, Due Date, Past Due, Amount, Open Balance.”
  • S2-R1: “Every column on all six reports sorts when its header is clicked, except A/P Unpaid Invoices' Vendor Name column (S2-N1). The columns are:”
  • S2-R2: “The first click gives the useful order for the kind of data: text (names, Location, Transaction Type) A to Z; money columns largest first; dates oldest first; Past Due largest first; ID and No. smallest number first (S2-R4). The second click reverses it. The third click repeats the first; there is no unsorted state.”
  • S2-R5: “On the grouped reports, a header click sorts the rows inside each group; the groups themselves never move (S1-R5, S1-R6).”
